Subject: FinServe RFP - data residency clarifications

Hi Jonas / Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the RFP. A couple of follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:

- We need a clear statement on whether any PII or model context for EU customers may be processed or stored outside the EU under your hosted offering.
- If cross-border processing is possible in exceptional cases, what explicit controls do you provide (consent, logging, ability to lock to region)?
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, what is the difference in control plane location and encryption key management?

I've attached our RFI spreadsheet with specific cells where we need a short answer and a supporting doc where applicable. Can we get initial responses by EOD Friday? If helpful, happy to do a 30m call to walk through.

Best,
Elena
Head of Infrastructure Risk
FinServe Corp

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Marissa (solutions) will provide the technical answers; I'll cover policy and contract-level items (DPA/SCCs).

Quick summary up-front so procurement has something to work with today:
- Hosted API (standard): primary processing in the region selected (we offer EU-only hosting in our eu-west clusters). By default we avoid cross-border processing for region-tagged requests; however customers can opt into cross-region fallback for availability reasons. That opt-in is explicit and requires an admin setting and consent in the contract.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools in customer-chosen region; control plane remains in the same region by default for Dedicated EU deployments.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full data plane and control plane can be customer-hosted — no Redwood-managed cross-border control plane unless explicitly agreed.

I'll attach the RFI answers and a short diagram (Marissa is consolidating). If you like, we can do a 30-minute technical sync tomorrow morning.

Hi Elena — attaching the completed RFI answers (see FinServe_RFI_answers_20260212.xlsx) and an architecture sketch (eu-hosting-architecture-20260212.png). Answers below are the condensed versions pulled from the spreadsheet.

1) Hosted API (multitenant / hosted):
- EU-only processing: Yes. We operate a set of EU regional clusters (eu-west-1 / eu-central-1). You can configure the tenant to pin to EU clusters and we will enforce regional routing at the edge. We log routing decisions and provide exportable audit trails.
- Cross-border fallback: Configurable per-tenant. Two modes:
  a) Strict geofencing: hard deny outbound requests if EU capacity is unavailable (recommended for customers with zero cross-border tolerance).
  b) Controlled failover: route to a compatible EU-semantics model hosted in a nearby non-EU region (e.g., UK/NO/US-east) only if customer has agreed to emergency fallback in contract; all such events generate immediate alerts and a detailed audit record.
- Data retention on cache / KV: by default ephemeral (token-level KV cached for performance) with configurable TTLs; persistent logs retained per agreed retention policy.

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- Dedicated GPU pools deployed into customer-selected region; control plane can be deployed in-region for EU Dedicated customers to avoid cross-border control-plane traffic.
- KMS: Customer-managed keys supported (bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM) for both data at rest and model cache encryption.

3) Private / On-Prem:
- Full air-gapped option available: deployment script + private control plane; no outbound telemetry unless customer enables.

4) Compliance & legal:
- We provide a standard DPA with SCCs included; SOC 2 Type II reports available under NDA.
- Data processing addendum notes: we can commit to EU data residency for processing and storage for named accounts via contract.

5) Operational controls & telemetry:
- Per-request region tag, token-level cost/latency logs, and a fallback event feed (webhook + Audit log export).
- Canary/fallback policies: per-deployment routing config, canary %s, and an option to require manual approval before any cross-border failover.

6) Implementation notes for FinServe (recommendation):
- Start with EU Dedicated for first-line production tenant (guaranteed capacity, in-region control plane)
- Add Private for regulated workloads that must be air-gapped
- For hosted dev/test, use EU-only hosted with strict geofencing enabled

If you'd like I can expand any spreadsheet cell into a short paragraph for the RFP. Happy to jump on a call with your security team tomorrow 10:00-10:30 CET.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachments: FinServe_RFI_answers_20260212.xlsx; eu-hosting-architecture-20260212.png; redwood-dpa-sccs-2025.pdf

Thanks Marissa — this is helpful. A few clarification points from our infra team:

- When you say "control plane in-region for Dedicated", does that include the job scheduler and metrics ingestion endpoints, or only the management API? We'd prefer metrics to stay in-region as well.
- For controlled failover, does the audit log include the full request transcript (redacted), or only metadata about which tenant/request was failed over? We need to know whether request payloads ever transit non-EU regions.
- For BYOK, can we rotate keys without downtime and can key access be restricted to our AWS account HSM only?

Would appreciate short answers; we'll insert into the RFP and come back with any redlines.

—Daniel

Subject: Re: FinServe RFP - data residency clarifications (follow-up)

Hi Daniel / Elena — quick follow-up with the clarifications you asked for: 

1) Control plane scope for Dedicated:
- We can run the full management stack (management API, job scheduler, metrics ingestion, logging collector) in-region for EU Dedicated deployments. Metrics ingestion endpoints will accept telemetry in-region and we support exporting metrics to customer-specified endpoints inside the customer's VPC.

2) Audit logs & failover transcript: 
- Primary behavior: audit events include metadata (tenant id, request id, timestamp, routing decision, failover flag).
- Request contents: request payloads are not stored long-term in plaintext. For debugging we can provide redacted request transcripts under strict access controls and only if enabled. For controlled failover, transcript access is a configurable option; by default we do NOT route raw request bodies outside the pinned region. Any explicit cross-border processing mode is surfaced in the audit and triggers a webhook + support ticket.

3) BYOK rotations and HSM restrictions:
- Key rotation: supported with zero-downtime for both Dedicated and Private deployments via our KMS rotation handshake; keys are versioned and active keys are referenced by ID to avoid blocking live workloads.
- AWS HSM: we support restricting key usage to customer AWS accounts (BYOK through customer-managed KMS in their account) for Dedicated and Private setups. Hosted tenants can also bring keys via a customer KMS federation model; details in the attached DPA doc.

Next steps:
- We'll send an updated RFI workbook with the short answers in-line (see attached).
- If FinServe requires a contractual hard-stop on any cross-border processing (i.e., no fallback under any circumstance), we can produce a special addendum for that commitment — this is typically offered on Dedicated + Private contracts.

If that addresses your items, Jonas and I can coordinate a legal + security call next week to finalize language.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
